finding.claim: Unauthenticated /fetch passes the raw target query parameter directly to http.Get with no validation, enabling full-response SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: main.go:15 r.URL.Query().Get("target") on unauthenticated route /fetch (registered main.go:41)

trace.note: target taken from query string, no parsing or validation
http.Get(target) issues outbound request to attacker-chosen URL
err.Error() reflected to client, giving connectivity oracle
io.Copy streams response body back to attacker

finding.guards_checked: None present. No scheme check, host allowlist, private/loopback IP check, redirect control, or auth. Go http.Get restricts scheme to http/https only.

verdict.guard_found: none. main.go:16 calls http.Get(target) on the raw query value from main.go:15 with no parsing, scheme, host, or IP check. The only allowlist (main.go:9-12, checked at main.go:27) is in safeFetch, which is registered on /safe (main.go:42), not on /fetch (main.go:41). No auth middleware is registered in main.go.
verdict.reason: The /fetch route (main.go:41) is unauthenticated, the target value comes straight from the query string (main.go:15) and is passed to http.Get (main.go:16) with no closing guard, and the response body is streamed back to the client (main.go:22), so an attacker can reach internal hosts and metadata endpoints. All trace lines match the file.

finding.claim: /safe enforces a hostname allowlist only on the initial URL; http.Get follows redirects by default, so an allowlisted host can redirect the server to internal or metadata URLs, bypassing the allowlist.
finding.source: main.go:26 r.URL.Query().Get("target") on unauthenticated route /safe (registered main.go:42)
finding.sink: main.go:31 http.Get(u.String()) with default client following redirects

trace.note: allowed[u.Hostname()] check applied to first URL only
http.Get uses DefaultClient with no CheckRedirect; follows up to 10 redirects to any host
io.Copy streams final redirected response body to attacker

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allowlist at main.go:27 is enforced and applies to the same u used at main.go:31; userinfo, port, case, and trailing-dot tricks fail closed. Not enforced: redirect hops (no CheckRedirect), resolved IP (no private-range check). Exploitability requires an open redirect or attacker-influenced response on images.example.org or docs.example.org, which could not be verified from this repo.

verdict.guard_found: main.go:27 is exact hostname membership (allowed[u.Hostname()]), but it runs only on the initial URL. The sink at main.go:31 is http.Get(u.String()) with the default client, which has no CheckRedirect, so redirect hops are not checked. No other validation exists on the path. The rejected-by-default checks (CheckRedirect, IP-range check) are absent.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: /safe is registered unauthenticated at main.go:42, the target query parameter reaches url.Parse at main.go:26, the allowlist check at main.go:27 covers only the first URL, and http.Get at main.go:31 follows redirects to any host with no CheckRedirect, with the response streamed back at main.go:37. The exploit still requires an allowlisted host (images.example.org or docs.example.org) to issue a redirect, which this repo cannot confirm, so the real-world severity depends on that external precondition.
